title: Adding and Removing Elements with jQuery
summary: Shows how jQuery can insert new HTML into a live page with before(), after(), prepend() and append(), and delete elements with remove(). The four insertion methods differ only in where the new markup lands relative to the selected element.

concepts.heading: Inserting elements: the four methods
points: Select an element with $(), then call an insertion method and pass it a string of HTML. jQuery parses the string, builds the element(s) and places them in the DOM; the source .html file is never modified, so a page refresh removes them.
before(html) inserts the new markup as a sibling immediately in front of the selected element's opening tag (outside it).
after(html) inserts the markup as a sibling immediately behind the selected element's closing tag (outside it).
prepend(html) inserts the markup inside the selected element, as its first child, right after the opening tag and before the existing content.
append(html) inserts the markup inside the selected element, as its last child, after the existing content but before the closing tag.

Rule of thumb: before/after place content outside the element; prepend/append place it inside. Inspecting the page in dev tools makes the difference visible: a button added with prepend sits inside the h1 ahead of the text, one added with append sits inside the h1 behind the text.
The demo uses '<button>New</button>' as the HTML string in each case, typed in the browser console against the live page.

concepts.heading: Removing elements
points: remove() deletes every element in the jQuery selection from the DOM. $('button').remove() clears all button elements on the page in one go.
(Extra) remove() also discards the elements' attached event handlers and data; detach() is the variant that keeps them for re-insertion later.
(Extra) Inserted HTML strings are real markup, so never build them from untrusted user input without escaping, or you open the door to script injection.

code_examples.caption: Insertion and removal methods on the h1 and buttons (matches the reference script)
code_examples.code:
$("button").remove();                      // delete all buttons
$("h1").before("<button>New</button>");     // sibling above the h1
$("h1").after("<button>New</button>");      // sibling below the h1
$("h1").prepend("<button>New</button>");    // inside h1, before the text
$("h1").append("<button>New</button>");     // inside h1, after the text

pitfalls: Confusing before/after (siblings) with prepend/append (children): a button prepended to an h1 becomes part of the heading.
Changes made this way live only in the running page; they vanish on reload because the HTML file is untouched.

In the reference repo the script lines are in the order remove, before, after, prepend, append; run remove() first and it will empty the page of the buttons that were there originally. The reference index.html also carries a personal footer credit that is not part of the lesson.

playground.coverage: No playground lesson yet (the playground has no jQuery section)
gaps_and_ideas: Proposed lesson 'jQuery: adding and removing elements'. Blurb: place new markup before, after, inside-start and inside-end of an element and delete nodes.

Tasks: 1) add a 'New' button above the h1 with before(); 2) add one below with after(); 3) use prepend and append and inspect where they land; 4) remove all buttons; 5) rebuild the same four placements with plain JS insertAdjacentHTML (beforebegin, afterend, afterbegin, beforeend) to compare.
Starter code: an h1 and five buttons plus a console-like input.
Interactive demo: a visual diagram of one box labelled 'h1' with four drop zones; clicking a method name highlights where the new element lands and shows the resulting HTML.
